description: Rubrics for the follow-up tasks, written with the tasks before any run; each example_pass is checked against its own rubric when loaded.

checks.description: later occurrences are computed by adding weeks in UTC
names extend_series as the renewal path
extend computes from the series' original first date
steps local dates / converts each occurrence with local_to_utc
flags the clash with already-booked rows (ADR 0013 / inconsistency)
the strict xfail / pinned HP-503 tests flip

must_not.description: claims ADR 0013 is accepted or implemented

F01.example_pass: Cause (HP-503): extend_series reuses occurrence_windows, which converts the series' original first_date with local_to_utc and then adds weeks in UTC, so a renewal after the October change lands at 18:00. Fix: step local dates from booking_series.local_start_time and convert each occurrence with local_to_utc. Risk: rows already booked keep the old UTC times, which ADR 0013 (still proposed) warns makes series inconsistent; find them by comparing each booking's local time with the series' local_start_time. The strict xfail tests and test_hp503 pin flip.

checks.description: names refund_preview
preview ignores the flag (use_v2=True hard-coded)
the v1 rule: 24 hours, full or nothing (V1_FULL / V1_NONE)
the real refund reads the flag when the booking is cancelled
flag values are cached, so a flip takes up to a minute
flipped via the superuser toggle (audited)

F05.example_pass: Not safe yet: refund_preview hard-codes use_v2=True, so the cancel page would keep showing v2 while refund_requested reads refund_policy_v2 at cancel time and pays v1 (V1_FULL at 24h or more, else V1_NONE). Fix refund_preview and the refund-preview endpoint first, add tests next to the v1-behind-flag tests. Flip via the superuser toggle_flag endpoint (audited); is_enabled caches flags for FLAG_CACHE_SECONDS, so allow a minute.

checks.description: uses the feature_flags table / ADR 0014
adds the flag in a migration, default off
checks it with flags.is_enabled
gates start_checkout / the checkout endpoint
flipped through the existing superuser toggle

F07.example_pass: Add a payments_paused flag row in a new migration with enabled = false, following ADR 0014 and the feature_flags INSERT pattern. In billing.payments.start_checkout (and so POST /checkout) check flags.is_enabled('payments_paused') and refuse with a friendly error. The duty manager flips it with the superuser toggle_flag endpoint (audited). Invoice customers never reach card checkout, so they are unaffected.

checks.description: changes verify_magic_link
adds a staff TTL setting next to magic_link_ttl_minutes
no schema change: last_login_at already exists (migration 0010)
names staff_users.last_login_at
records logins with write_audit / audit_log
updates the auth tests

F10.example_pass: No schema change: migration 0010 already added staff_users.last_login_at. Add staff_magic_link_ttl_minutes (10) next to magic_link_ttl_minutes in config and use it in verify_magic_link for staff links; record each staff login with write_audit and set last_login_at. Update test_auth (test_staff_link_can_be_reused documents the old gap).

checks.description: calls reconcile_day
exceptions are stored with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
the email is deduplicated per day
finance-only endpoint via require_role
links it to HP-489 / missed days

F12.example_pass: Add POST /reconciliation/<day> in api/staff.py guarded by require_role(finance, superuser), like invoices/run, calling reconcile_day for that day. Re-runs are safe: _store inserts reconciliation_exceptions with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and _email_finance uses dedupe key recon:<day>, so one email per day. Also useful for the HP-489 missed days backfill.
